title: AlphaFold3 modeling supports a functional COG4–Syntaxin 5 interface
summary: A preprint abstract reports that AlphaFold3 modeling placed COG4 against a Syntaxin5 loop/linker region, supporting a proposed interface in Golgi membrane trafficking. Targeted substitutions, co-precipitation and cell-based rescue assays linked that interface to protein glycosylation and Golgi organization. This is an abstract-scoped source check: full Methods, sample sizes and detailed controls were inaccessible, and no organism-level or clinical effect is established.
organization: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports targeted interface substitutions, co-precipitation, rescue, glycosylation, localization and Golgi-morphology assays in cells.
evidence.unknown: Full Methods, sample sizes and detailed experimental controls were not assessed because primary full-text routes were inaccessible. The reviewed material does not establish organism-level or clinical effects.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold3 predicted a COG4–Syntaxin5 contact arrangement; the reported cell perturbations test the functional interface described by that model.

source_review.scope: Complete publisher-deposited Crossref and bioRxiv v1 abstracts, posted date and author affiliations; full primary PDF/XML access attempts were blocked, so full Methods were not read.
